html:
A surprise attack by Japanese carrier aircraft on the US Pacific Fleet at Pearl Harbor, Hawaii, on the morning of 7 December 1941. About 2,400 Americans were killed, and all eight battleships in the harbour were damaged, four of them sunk.

Japan was at war in China and had moved into French Indochina. The United States answered with an oil embargo, and Japan's leaders decided to seize the oil and rubber of Southeast Asia, above all the Dutch East Indies. The attack was meant to stop the US fleet from interfering. Japan struck the Philippines, Malaya and Hong Kong at about the same time.

The raid missed the American aircraft carriers, which were at sea, and the fuel tanks and repair yards. President Franklin D. Roosevelt called it "a date which will live in infamy", and Congress declared war the next day. Germany declared war on the United States days later, joining the Pacific and European wars into one world war. Six months later the US Navy won at Midway, and the war ended with the atomic bombings of 1945.
